page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Pushed to the limits
title: Pushed to the limits
topic: Language to use when trying to set priorities
description:
At the offices of Tip Top Trading, things are a bit tricky. Denise has been reinstated at the company but now wants to do more than just ordering pens. Tom has other ideas and Anna is just caught in the middle. She needs to get organised and get her priorities straight!
This episode focuses on the language that you might use or hear when you are busy at work and need to set priorities.
phrases: I've got to prioritise. This task is the most important so I'm going to concentrate on this first.
It would be a great help if you could do this for me please.
I'm going to have to put that off until tomorrow I'm afraid.

listening_challenge.question: When is Anna going to look at the designs for the plastic aubergine?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work. At the offices of Tip Top Trading, things are a bit… tricky. Denise has been reinstated at the company but now wants to do more than just ordering pens. Tom has other ideas and Anna is just caught in the middle. Who can she turn to? Paul maybe… or maybe not?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So Denise, let's get this straight. You don't want to order the pens anymore, right?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well, I did say if I came back, I wanted to have a go at doing sales.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Err, yes, you did. That's right.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah but we got Denise back because we didn't have anyone to order our pens and stuff. That's her main job.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Err yes, absolutely. I see your point.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Excuse me Paul, could I suggest we all take it in turns to order things like pens and paper… share the responsibility?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That's a good idea Anna.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah but…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No buts Tom, that's a good solution. Well done Anna… could you draw up a rota so we know who's going to be ordering the pens and when? And don't forget to order biscuits too! Phew, I'm glad I got that sorted out. Right, back to work everyone.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I can't believe I've got to order pens, it's Denise's responsibility… err, are you OK Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No I'm not. I can't draw up a rota, not now. I've got too much to do.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Alright don't panic Anna. Just do what I do.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What's that?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Nothing! Just do what you can do and then pretend you've forgotten about the other stuff. Easy!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear, Tom's not that professional is he? Not like you Anna. You just need to get organised and prioritise.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I need to prioritise?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes. Decide what tasks need doing first and maybe delegate some tasks to others. You could say to people "I've got to prioritise. This is the most important so I'm going to concentrate on this first.", then you could say to someone "It would be a great help if you could take on this other task". You could also say "I'll have to put off some tasks until tomorrow". And if you still feel under pressure, say to your boss "I need help, I have too much to do".

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks, good advice. I'm just writing a list of all the things I need to do on my new mini me-pad.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Writing a list is a good place to start. Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: There, that's my list finished. Ah, Denise, sorry to bother you, but you know that rota I was talking about?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: The one for ordering pens?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's it. Well, I'm so busy, I was wondering… it would be a great help… if you could make a start on this? Please?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Of course Anna. As it's you. If it was Tom asking, I would have said no!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What's that Denise? Hey Anna, what are we going to do about the designs for that plastic aubergine?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Gosh, our new aubergine. Hmm, I'm going to have to put that off until tomorrow I'm afraid.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh right. Why, have you got something more important for us to do together, eh?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No Tom. I've just got to prioritise. This new order from Nice'n'Cheesy is the most important, so I'm going to concentrate on that first. OK?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh right, yeah sure. Me and you will have to wait until tomorrow! So… so… how's it going with Dave from Computer Support?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Very well thanks Tom. Last night he took me somewhere I've never been to before.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Really. Nice.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, a discount computer shop – he bought me a mini me-pad.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh. Just a 'mini' one hey.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Now, if you could take more interest in our Nice'n'Cheesy contract than you do in Dave, it would be a great help.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yeah, sure, of course… nice'n'sleazy, that's a good name for Dave!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Idiot! Getting organised is important when you have a lot to do. Tell people what you're doing and don't forget to ask for help. Here's a reminder of what Anna said:
I've got to prioritise. This task is the most important so I'm going to concentrate on this first.
It would be a great help if you could do this for me please.
I'm going to have to put that off until tomorrow I'm afraid.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And don't forget, when you simply have too much to do, tell your boss!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hello Paul, sorry to bother you. I'm a bit worried… I just have too much to do and need some help.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes of course. I don't want you feeling stressed. Let me think… erm... I know, why don't I do the pen rota?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's OK, Denise has offered to do that.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Phew, I mean super! Erm… hmm… well, maybe Tom could help you with the launch party?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Launch party? What launch party?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Didn't Tom tell you?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, he didn't.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: We're launching the plastic aubergine on Friday.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Keep calm Anna! We're here to help – although organising a launch party in a week is quite a challenge. Find out how it goes on the next English at Work. Bye!
